title: Double-decker luminescent ytterbium and erbium SMMs with symmetric and asymmetric Schiff base ligands

material_class.structural_family: double-decker Schiff-base cluster with associated Er(NO3)3

synthesis.procedure: A stirred acetonitrile solution of AZOL and Er(NO3)3·xH2O was heated under reflux. After addition of Et3N the colour changed from brown to dark red and a precipitate formed. The mixture was stirred and refluxed for 6 h. The precipitate was filtered, washed with hot acetonitrile, and dried with anhydrous diethyl ether.

reagents.name: triethylamine
reagents.amount: 81 mL (0.868 mmol; likely μL by stoichiometry)

synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Precipitate filtered, washed with hot acetonitrile, dried with anhydrous diethyl ether. Isolated as a powder; single crystals were not obtained.

properties.summary: Field-induced Er(III) SMM: no out-of-phase AC signal to 1.8 K at zero DC field; tails of χ″ appear for DC fields >1000 Oe. χT at 300 K matches four Er(III) ions and decreases on cooling, especially below 50 K. Ligand-centred fluorescence is quenched (CHEQ; QY <0.1%). Direct excitation at 590 nm gives weak NIR emission centred at 1475 nm (4I13/2 → 4I15/2); 300–500 nm ligand excitation does not produce the expected Er NIR band.

measurements.conditions: 2–300 K; DC fields 3000 and 300 Oe; non-field-dependent χT

measurements.conditions: AC susceptibility; field-induced SMM

material_class.structural_family: double-decker Schiff-base cluster with associated Yb(NO3)3

synthesis.procedure: A stirred acetonitrile solution of AZOL and Yb(NO3)3·5H2O was heated under reflux. After addition of Et3N the colour changed from brown to dark red and a precipitate formed. The mixture was stirred and refluxed for 6 h. The precipitate was filtered, washed with hot acetonitrile, and dried with anhydrous diethyl ether.
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Precipitate filtered, washed with hot acetonitrile, dried with anhydrous diethyl ether. Isolated as a powder; single crystals were not obtained.

properties.summary: Not an SMM: no χ″ to 1.8 K at zero DC field and AZOL does not provide a suitable crystal field for field-induced SMM behaviour. χT at 300 K matches four Yb(III) and decreases smoothly on cooling. Ligand fluorescence is quenched (QY <0.1%). NIR Yb emission is observed: narrow 2F5/2 → 2F7/2 band at 976 nm (solid, λex 420 nm) plus crystal-field sidebands; also seen in 2×10^-5 M CH3CN.

measurements.name: χT vs T
measurements.value: in agreement with four Yb(III) (2F7/2, gJ = 8/7) at 300 K
measurements.conditions: 2–300 K; DC fields 3000 and 300 Oe

measurements.value: no χ″ down to 1.8 K without DC field; not SMM

measurements.conditions: solid state, RT; λex 420 nm (also 480 nm in Fig. 5); 2F5/2 → 2F7/2; also in 2×10^-5 M CH3CN

synthesis.procedure: A stirred acetonitrile solution of SYML, Er(NO3)3·xH2O and Et3N was heated under reflux for 6 h. After 5–6 days, orange crystals of SYML–Er2 formed by slow evaporation.

reagents.name: triethylamine
reagents.amount: 100 mL, 0.6 mmol (volume likely μL by stoichiometry)

synthesis.vessel_or_method: reflux then slow evaporation of CH3CN
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Orange crystals by slow evaporation of the acetonitrile reaction mixture.

properties.summary: Field-induced Er SMM: χ″ tail at zero DC field; at 2000 Oe, slow-relaxation χ″ peaks below 3 K plus a faster/QTM tail; AC data could not be fitted to a simple Debye model. DC χT decreases on cooling; PHI fit gives J = −0.24 cm−1 and MJ splitting ≈590 cm−1. UV-vis: λmax 331 and 395 nm. Ligand emission quenched (QY 0.3% vs 0.8% free SYML). Weak Er NIR emission at 1490 nm upon 590 nm excitation; 300–500 nm ligand excitation does not give 4I13/2 → 4I15/2.

synthesis.procedure: A stirred acetonitrile solution of SYML, Yb(NO3)3·5H2O and Et3N was heated under reflux for 6 h. After one day, orange crystals of SYML–Yb2 formed by slow evaporation.

reagents.amount: 100 mL, 0.6 mmol (volume likely μL by stoichiometry)

synthesis.vessel_or_method: reflux then slow evaporation of CH3CN
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Orange crystals by slow evaporation of the acetonitrile reaction mixture.

properties.summary: Field-induced Yb SMM: no χ″ peak at zero DC field; at 2000 Oe, frequency-dependent χ″ (1.8–5 K) fitted to Debye (α = 0.01 at 5 K to 0.34 at 1.8 K); Arrhenius Ueff = 5.5 K (1.8–2.3 K). PHI fit used J = 0; MJ splitting 793 cm−1. UV-vis: λmax 331 and 388 nm. Ligand QY 0.3%. Characteristic Yb NIR band at 976 nm (λex 420 nm) with ~700 cm−1 crystal-field sidebands; also in 2×10^-5 M CH3CN.

material_class.structural_family: trinuclear Schiff-base double-decker anion with 2-aminopyridinium counterion

synthesis.procedure: A stirred acetonitrile solution of SYML, Yb(NO3)3·5H2O and Et3N was refluxed for 6 h. Excess 2-aminopyridine was added to the cooled solution. After 5–7 days yellow crystals of SYML–Yb3 formed together with orange SYML–Yb2 and were separated by hand. Yields of the yellow product were always very poor (<5%).

reagents.name: triethylamine
reagents.amount: 100 mL, 0.6 mmol (volume likely μL by stoichiometry)

synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Yellow crystals hand-picked from a mixture with orange SYML–Yb2 and characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction.

properties.summary: The paper states that poor yields and co-crystallization with SYML–Yb2 precluded property studies of SYML–Ln3.

source_locations.location: LEJNIA matches Yb3 anion C112H72N10O14Yb3 with 2-aminopyridinium
